binding_constraint.reason: OIDC wiring (id-token: write + npm Trusted Publishing registration + Sigstore Fulcio trust on the repo) is the prerequisite for the entire signing surface. Without it: npm publish cannot produce provenance (blocks S5), cosign keyless cannot run (blocks S1, S2), SLSA reusable workflow cannot attest (blocks S3). 8 downstream RTs (RT-4, RT-5, RT-6, RT-8, RT-9 signing, RT-10 verify, RT-18, RT-19) depend on it. Hardest to verify-right the first time because OIDC audience/subject mismatches fail silently.

gap_checklist_compliance.note: Core data path is the CI release pipeline (tag commit -> build -> sign -> publish). Crosses boundaries: GitHub Actions -> npm registry, -> GHCR, -> Sigstore Fulcio. Covered by T5, O3, S1, S2, S5, O5.

Crypto/auth surface = cosign keyless signing (S1), npm OIDC trusted publishing (B1, S5), Sigstore provenance (S5). Attack matrix to generate in m4: signature-by-tag attack (prevented by digest binding), OIDC audience confusion, stale signature after rebuild.

gap_checklist_compliance.skip_reason: This feature distributes artifacts; it does not expose unauthenticated endpoints. Resource exhaustion relevant to npm/GHCR is the provider's concern, not ours.

gap_checklist_compliance.note: External dependencies: npm registry, GHCR, Sigstore (Fulcio + Rekor), crates used by cosign/trivy. Resilience addressed by O5 (retry/backoff on transient failures). No circuit breaker (one-shot release pipeline, not a long-running service).
JSON Schema for mock config (T6) is the input-validation contract for mock files. Schema is the consumer-side boundary; runtime validation is the Tier 1 manifold's concern.

CI matrix builds 4 binary targets in parallel (T3); no shared mutable state across jobs. Concurrent `npm publish` is prevented by the tag being the atomic trigger (only one workflow run per tag). No shared-state constraints in this feature.
